headline: US Consumer Spending Flattens as Energy and Transportation Costs Rise
summary: U.S. consumer spending rose sharply in September, but the increase primarily reflected higher household expenditures on gas and transportation following an energy cost surge.
why: Consumer spending drives roughly two-thirds of U.S. GDP. Shifts toward essential costs like fuel can squeeze discretionary household spending and influence Federal Reserve policy.

impacts.name: U.S. Retail
impacts.why: Higher spending on energy and transportation leaves less disposable income for discretionary goods.
